titleEn: I Have Two Feet, Momo Has Four!

pages.text: "Wait, Momo!" Wearing a vermilion scarf, Yuki ran with both hands on the ground. Slippery leaves sent their legs sliding—thump! Leaves covered their sleeves.
Brown dog Momo was already barking from the slope above. "I want to run fast like Momo!" Yuki put both hands down again.
Another slip! This time, leaves covered the knees, too. Momo climbed so well on four feet. "Why do I keep falling?" Yuki's shoulders drooped.
Grandma came down in gray layered clothes, carrying dry branches. "What's worrying you?" "I'm slower than Momo."
Grandma pointed toward the sun. Two shadows lay together on the leaves, one broad and one tall. "Whose is broad, and whose is tall?"
"The tall one's mine, because I'm standing! Momo's is broad because of four feet." Yuki pointed to each. "I Have Two Feet, Momo Has Four!"
Standing on two feet left two hands free. Yuki gathered an armful of leaves and tossed them high. They showered down while Momo hopped beneath them.
Momo reached the top first and barked. Holding a branch with both hands, Yuki placed a foot on the hilltop's edge. "Just a little more!"
Yuki hugged Momo with one arm and fixed the scarf knot with the other. "One, I hug with two hands! Two, Momo climbs with four feet! Three, help each other do what we can't!"
Grandma hugged Yuki tightly and stroked their back. Being different meant each could help with what the other could not do. Yuki kicked leaves into the air. "I Have Two Feet, Momo Has Four!"
